LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 12.3.1 QUESTION TAGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.3: Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What is a question tag? 2. How do we form question tags?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  In purposive groups, identify the verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals,  Form tag questions using verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals. Learners with speech difficulties could be allowed extra time to make presentations  Apply rules

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  In purposive groups, identify the verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals,  Form tag questions using verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals. Learners with speech difficulties could be allowed extra time to make presentations  Apply rules

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration: The learner’s ability to work with peers is enhanced as they practice using tag questions in dialogues and

conversations.

Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to manipulate digital devices is improved as they search for more examples of question

tags on the internet.

Values:
Love is fostered as the learner portrays a caring attitude while collaborating with peers to display posters on tag questions in

class.

Respect is inculcated as the learner displays patience while searching for examples of question tags on the web, with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Environmental Conservation (Environment Education): The learner is able to communicate to others about environmental

conservation practices using tag questions in dialogues and conversations.

 Life Skills (Creativity): The learner displays creativity as they form tag questions using verbs to be, verbs to have verbs to

do and modals.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner is able to relate the skills of using question tags to the learning of interrogatives in Kiswahili.
